do_not_assume: Missing notification email means no exception occurred.
Every exception is a software defect; page and block misconfiguration are also documented causes.
goal: Identify the narrowest supported failure boundary without claiming an unverified root cause.
steps: Open the Exception List and locate the grouped exception type.
Record the recurrence count and relevant timestamps.
Open a detail record and identify the associated page, block, job, or action.
Correlate the first occurrence with recent configuration or version changes.
Check official release notes for the installed version.
Reproduce only through a bounded, non-destructive path.
Verify that the exception stops recurring after the demonstrated cause is corrected.
title: Recipe: Triage a recurring exception

do_not_assume: The linked-key count must decrease after a tag clear.
A global cache clear will regenerate a Persisted Dataset.
goal: Refresh the affected output without unnecessarily clearing unrelated caches.
steps: Identify the stale block and its caching mode.
Open its settings and identify assigned cache tags.
Open Cache Manager.
Clear the most specific applicable tag.
Reload the affected page and confirm that the intended content changed.
If it remains stale, determine whether the data comes from a Persisted Dataset or another cache layer before taking broader action.
title: Recipe: Refresh stale cached output with minimum scope

do_not_assume: Similar block names imply that blocks share a cache.
A tag can be renamed later. Add Cache Tags
goal: Establish a durable, targeted invalidation boundary for related cached blocks.
steps: Define the content group whose caches should be invalidated together.
Choose a short lowercase name without spaces.
Write a description that explains the tag’s intended scope.
Add the tag in `Admin Tools > CMS Configuration > Cache Manager`.
Open each caching-enabled block in scope and assign the tag.
Test the relationship by changing non-sensitive content, clearing the tag, and verifying all intended blocks.
Record the tag as permanent because the documentation says it cannot be modified or deleted.
title: Recipe: Create and assign a cache tag

do_not_assume: A false `Incomplete` row on an affected version proves the job failed.
A successful history row proves the intended business records changed.
goal: Determine whether recorded executions match the expected schedule and whether the downstream result is current.
steps: Identify the exact scheduled job.
Inspect several consecutive history records.
Compare expected schedule with start and stop timestamps.
Review status, status message, and duration.
Check whether the installed version is affected by the v19.5 job-history defects.
Inspect the job’s downstream artifact, such as index freshness, automated record changes, or persisted data.
Report history status and downstream verification separately.
Inspect the job’s expected schedule and its most recent consecutive history rows.
Compare start time, stop time, status, status message, and duration rather than relying on the last status label alone.
Check whether the installed version predates the v19.5 fix for jobs silently stopping after errors while recording status, writing history, or sending notifications.
If rows are duplicated, falsely `Incomplete`, or show implausible durations for extremely fast work, check applicability of the separate v19.5 sub-second-history fix.
Verify the downstream result independently; history recording and business work are related but not identical outcomes.
Stop when version applicability or the installed job configuration cannot be established without live review. Rock release notes
title: Recipe: Audit a scheduled job’s recent health

do_not_assume: A record in Rock is automatically eligible for Universal Search.
Attribute security carries into Universal Search.
Re-indexing corrects a wrong provider or eligibility setting.
goal: Return one known eligible record to search without rebuilding unrelated indexes first.
steps: Verify provider connectivity.
Confirm the entity is enabled.
Confirm the entity-specific eligibility setting.
Confirm that intended attributes are permitted and safe to index.
Inspect the relevant re-index or site-crawl job.
Correct connectivity or eligibility before initiating a bulk operation.
Run the supported entity-specific bulk load or allow the scheduled job to complete.
Search for one known eligible record and verify its destination URL.
Confirm that Person indexing is enabled.
Confirm that the specific attribute is selected for indexing.
Assess whether the attribute is safe to expose, because Universal Search does not enforce person-attribute security.
Run the supported Person bulk load or wait for the nightly re-index.
If the installed version predates v19.3, check applicability of the documented Person Attribute Values defect.
Stop if the desired attribute is sensitive or version applicability is unknown. Specifics for Entities
title: Recipe: Restore a missing Universal Search entity

do_not_assume: Unlinked pages will be discovered.
The nightly Universal Search Re-Index job crawls Site entities.
Hiding a link page from navigation alone provides the documented security boundary.
goal: Index the intended site pages without unintentionally exposing or omitting secured content.
steps: Enable indexing in the site’s advanced settings.
Choose a crawling starting location that links to every intended page.
If secured content is required, use a dedicated crawler identity and restrict the link page to that identity and administrators.
Ensure the crawler cannot access a logout action that would terminate its session.
Configure an `Index Rock Site` job with the intended schedule.
Inspect job history after execution.
Verify representative public and authorized results separately.
title: Recipe: Configure a bounded site-index crawl

do_not_assume: A high confidence score proves identity.
The primary record automatically supplies the correct address.
Access to start a merge means access to complete it.
goal: Merge only records demonstrated to belong to the same person while preserving the intended values.
steps: Open the pair in Duplicate Finder.
Compare identity evidence and Record Source.
Review Account Protection Profile and operator permissions.
If uncertain, defer rather than merge.
If confirmed, select the primary record.
Review each surviving value, including the address separately.
Submit a Merge Request if the operator lacks merge authority.
Verify the resulting profile and any expected notification after completion.
title: Recipe: Review and resolve a duplicate-person candidate

do_not_assume: A Data View name proves its current membership logic.
Person inactivation affects only the person’s Active flag.
The documented Tuesday schedule is still configured locally.
Do not rerun the job until the criteria and downstream effects are understood.
goal: Define the expected affected population and side effects before a job mutates records.
steps: Identify the exact automation function being changed.
Inspect all inclusion and exclusion Data Views.
Inspect inactive-reason restrictions when reactivation is involved.
Review effects on family structure, campus, connection status, family status, groups, security roles, and launched workflows as applicable.
Review the maximum records processed per run.
Record the expected population and expected field changes.
Obtain authorization before saving material changes or running the job.
After execution, compare job history and a bounded sample of resulting records.
Identify which automation function changed the records.
Inspect its inclusion and exclusion Data Views, inactive-reason settings, and processing limit.
Check whether affected people were also changed in groups or security roles.
Correlate the changes with the Data Automation job’s execution history and audit information already available.
Do not rerun the job until the criteria and downstream effects are understood.
If temporary auditing is proposed, account for its significant performance cost. Use Data Automation
title: Recipe: Review a Data Automation change before execution
